title: Add wrapper module modules/redwood-private-vpc with stable networking outputs
author: Bruno Silva
description:
This PR introduces a wrapper module `modules/redwood-private-vpc` that composes the alpha building blocks (`vpc-baseline`, `vpc-endpoints`, `security-groups-baseline`) and presents a stable outputs contract for the Redwood Private installer + examples. Motivation: we want customers and PS to have a single “happy path” module with validated defaults, while keeping the underlying modules usable independently.

Key design points: The wrapper intentionally narrows the surface area: it wires opinionated defaults (subnet tiering, endpoint defaults, tags), but keeps escape hatches for existing VPC adoption and locked-down egress. The outputs are explicitly treated as an installer contract and are documented + versioned (breaking changes require SemVer major in this wrapper). We also add validation to prevent known foot-guns (e.g., enabling private-only endpoints without resolver/DNS support; requesting endpoints while consuming externally-managed subnets without providing required route table ids).

Stable outputs contract (v0.x alpha): - vpc_id - subnet_ids_by_tier (public/private/isolated) - private_subnet_ids (alias for installer) - isolated_subnet_ids (alias for data-plane-only deployments) - route_table_ids_by_tier (when managed) - vpc_endpoint_ids + vpc_endpoint_dns_entries (selected interface endpoints) - security_group_ids (control_plane, data_plane, endpoints) - nat_mode + nat_gateway_ids (when applicable) - flow_logs_destination (cloudwatch|s3|disabled) + log_group_arn / s3_bucket_arn

Defaults: - Endpoint set defaults to: S3 (gateway), ECR API/DKR, CloudWatch Logs. STS/SSM remain opt-in for now (see notes) but output wiring supports them. - `enable_private_dns` defaults true for interface endpoints. - Tags merge: module-level tags + required Redwood tags (owner, env, cost-center, data-class).

Notes / follow-ups: - STS endpoint likely becomes required for “no public egress” installs (installer preflight is being updated separately). We intentionally keep it optional here but call it out prominently in README and example tfvars. - This wrapper does not attempt to manage NACLs; it documents expected NACL posture and relies on SG baseline.

Testing: - `terraform fmt` + `terraform validate` on all modules - tflint/checkov run in CI - integration plan/apply harness updated to include wrapper module scenario (single NAT + per-AZ NAT).

Docs: Adds a README for the wrapper with a module matrix, example usage, and an explicit “installer contract” section.

Screenshots/logs: Included in CI summary below.

Checklist: - [x] variables have descriptions, types, and validation - [x] outputs documented and treated as contract - [x] terraform-docs generated - [x] examples compile - [x] CI green (tflint/checkov/integration apply)
commits: modules/redwood-private-vpc: initial wrapper skeleton + wiring baseline/endpoints/sg
outputs: define installer contract outputs + add aliases for legacy naming
validation: guard against incompatible existing-VPC combinations
docs: add README + terraform-docs generation for wrapper
ci: include wrapper in integration matrix (nat=single, nat=per-az)
ci_summary: Initial run: ❌ terraform-integration (us-east-2, nat=per-az) failed due to endpoint association ordering; fixed by adding explicit depends_on between wrapper endpoint SG attachment and endpoint resources; rerun ✅. Final: ✅ fmt/validate, ✅ tflint, ✅ checkov (2 suppressions with justification carried forward), ✅ integration apply (2 regions x 2 nat modes).
review_conversation: Irene Choi: Outputs contract looks good. Can we avoid returning nested maps that change shape depending on whether subnets are managed vs existing? The installer wants predictable keys.

Bruno Silva (author): Agree. I changed `route_table_ids_by_tier` to always be present with keys public/private/isolated; values are empty lists when in existing-VPC mode and we also output a boolean `managed_route_tables` for clarity. README updated with examples.

Ethan Park: For installer integration we need: vpc_id, private_subnet_ids, endpoint DNS names (ECR API/DKR, logs) and SG IDs. Please confirm these are stable and add an explicit 'Installer contract' section in wrapper README.

Bruno Silva (author): Added 'Installer contract (alpha)' section listing required outputs + naming guarantees. Also added `vpc_endpoint_dns_entries` in a stable list-of-objects-ish shape, but Terraform forces it to be a map; I documented the keys and added an output `ecr_api_endpoint_dns` / `ecr_dkr_endpoint_dns` as simple strings to keep the installer simple.

Marcus Lin: Security: by default, do we allow 0.0.0.0/0 egress from data-plane SG? We should be explicit. Also confirm private DNS defaults to true for interface endpoints and we don't accidentally open endpoint policies.

Bruno Silva (author): Updated wrapper defaults to keep SG baseline behavior (egress restricted to VPC CIDR + required AWS prefix lists when using gateway endpoints). Added README note: if customer requires strict egress, set `restrict_egress=true` and provide allowed destinations. Private DNS defaults true; endpoint policies remain 'allow all' stubs until we land least-privilege policies in a follow-up PR (called out).
Sahana Iyer: Integration job flaked in nat=per-az scenario with endpoint creation eventual consistency. Can we add ordering / retries? At least make it deterministic.

Bruno Silva (author): Added explicit `depends_on` where we were implicitly relying on provider graph. Also increased the harness retry around `terraform apply` once. Reruns stable on 6 consecutive runs in CI.
Benji Okafor: Nit: please align output names with what installer expects (`control_plane_sg_id` vs `controlplane_sg_id`).

Bruno Silva (author): Renamed outputs to `control_plane_sg_id`, `data_plane_sg_id`, `endpoints_sg_id` and kept backward-compatible aliases with deprecation notes in README. Marked aliases for removal in next minor after installer cutover.
release_notes: Terraform: Added `modules/redwood-private-vpc` wrapper module composing VPC baseline + endpoints + security groups and exposing a documented stable outputs contract for Redwood Private installer integrations.
